name: Shringasaurus
currentFacts: Features a pair of prominent forward-facing horns over its eyes, similar to modern ceratopsians.
Demonstrates sexual dimorphism with horns likely used in combat.

name: Gigantophis garstini
currentFacts: For over a century until the discovery of Titanoboa in 2009, Gigantophis was considered the largest known snake to have ever existed.
Historically estimated at 9 to 10 meters, a 2004 reassessment by Jason Head et al. revised its estimated length downward to approximately 6.9 ± 0.3 meters.
Belongs to the extinct family Madtsoiidae, sharing a deep evolutionary lineage with other giant Paleogene snakes such as Vasuki and Madtsoia.

name: Eoraptor lunensis
currentFacts: One of the earliest true dinosaurs.

name: Elaphrosaurus bambergi
currentFacts: Extremely long neck and slender body.

name: Dysalotosaurus lettowvorbecki
currentFacts: Thousands of bones in single bonebed.

name: Australodocus bohetii
currentFacts: Named for head local excavator Boheti.

name: Massospondylus carinatus
currentFacts: Fossilized eggs containing embryos with tiny teeth.

name: Eocursor parvus
currentFacts: One of the earliest known ornithischian dinosaurs.

name: Rebbachisaurus garasbae
currentFacts: Tall paddle-like ridge along back neural spines.

name: Onchopristis numidus
currentFacts: Barb-like teeth along sides of saw.

name: Alanqa saharica
currentFacts: Bony eminence along jaw margin for crushing hard shell prey.

name: Siroccopteryx moroccensis
currentFacts: Fine teeth for catching slippery fish.

name: Aegisuchus witmeri
currentFacts: Nicknamed Shieldcroc due to flat vascularized shield on top of head.

name: Lystrosaurus murrayi
currentFacts: Made up over 95% of terrestrial vertebrates post-extinction.

name: Moschops capensis
currentFacts: Pachyostotic thick head roof up to 10 cm for headbutting.

name: Diictodon feliceps
currentFacts: Burrowing dicynodont synapsid with spiral burrows.

name: Rubidgea atrox
currentFacts: Largest apex gorgonopsian saber-tooth in South Africa.

name: Procynosuchus delaharpeae
currentFacts: One of the earliest semi-aquatic cynodonts.

name: Anteosaurus magnificus
currentFacts: Thickened skull roof for head-butting rivals.

name: Australovenator wintonensis
currentFacts: Apex megaraptorid predator of Cretaceous Australia.

name: Diamantinasaurus matildae
currentFacts: Found alongside Australovenator in Matilda site.

name: Australotitan cooperensis
currentFacts: Largest dinosaur species ever discovered in Australia.

name: Isisfordia duncani
currentFacts: Oldest ancestor of modern true crocodiles (Eusuchia).

name: Ferrodraco lentoni
currentFacts: Most complete pterosaur skeleton from Australia.
Large crest at front of upper jaw.

name: Muttaburrasaurus langdoni
currentFacts: Hollow inflatable nasal chamber for vocal resonance.

name: Rapator ornithestoid
currentFacts: Opalized hand bone showing massive claw.
Found in Lightning Ridge opal mines.

name: Fostoria dhimbangunmal
currentFacts: First opalized dinosaur herd in the world.

name: Weewarrasaurus pobeni
currentFacts: Found in Wee Warra opal mine.

name: Lightningclaw
currentFacts: Largest theropod discovered in Australia prior to Australovenator.

name: Steropodon galmani
currentFacts: First Mesozoic mammal found in Australia.

name: Kollikodon ritchiei
currentFacts: Molar teeth with rounded crushing cusps.

name: Irritator challengeri
currentFacts: Received its name because paleontologists were immensely irritated by fossil poachers vandalizing the skull with plaster.
A tooth belonging to Irritator was found embedded inside a fossilized pterosaur spine, confirming pterosaur predation.
Possessed an exceptionally fast jaw closure mechanism, lowering its lower jaw sideways to swallow fish whole.

name: Brasileodactylus araripensis
currentFacts: Long jaw with expanding front teeth.

name: Tupuxuara longicristatus
currentFacts: Massive head crest growing with age.

name: Ludodactylus sibbicki
currentFacts: Unique leaf stuck in jaw specimen.

name: Neovenator salerii
currentFacts: Apex carcharodontosaurian of Early Cretaceous Europe.

name: Iguanodon bernissartensis
currentFacts: Large conical thumb spike for defense.

name: Caulkicephalus trimicrodon
currentFacts: Front teeth pointing forward for catching fish.

name: Valdosaurus canaliculatus
currentFacts: Femur with deep anterior intercondylar groove.

name: Concavenator corcovatus
currentFacts: Had two unusually tall neural spines above its hips forming a pointed crest or hump on its back.
Possessed quill knobs (apophysis) on its ulna, indicating the presence of proto-feather structures or displays on its arms.
One of the best preserved carcharodontosaurids ever discovered in Europe.

name: Pelecanimimus polychrodon
currentFacts: Soft tissue throat pouch preserved like a pelican.

name: Ornithopsis hulkei
currentFacts: Named based on bird-like bone honeycomb.

name: Kukufeldia tilgatensis
currentFacts: Mandible with distinctive neurovascular foramina pattern.
From historic Cuckfield quarry where Gideon Mantell worked.

name: Sinosauropteryx prima
currentFacts: First non-avian dinosaur discovered with preserved feathers.
Melanosome analysis confirmed reddish-brown striped tail.

name: Confuciusornis sanctus
currentFacts: Toothless beak in an early bird.
Pair of extremely long ribbon-like tail feathers in males.

name: Caudipteryx zhoui
currentFacts: Symmetrical true vane feathers on short tail and arms.
Swallowed gizzard stones (gastroliths) to grind food.

name: Repenomamus giganteus
currentFacts: Fossilized stomach contained remains of a juvenile Psittacosaurus.

name: Liaoningosaurus paradoxus
currentFacts: Fish skeletons preserved inside abdominal cavity.

name: Poposaurus gracilis
currentFacts: Found in Chinle and Popo Agie beds.

name: Stenopterygius quadriscissus
currentFacts: Preserved soft tissue outlines and dorsal fin.
Pregnant specimens with embryos inside birth canal.

name: Eurhinosaurus longirostris
currentFacts: Upper jaw twice length of lower jaw.

name: Seirocrinus subangularis
currentFacts: Largest sea lily crinoid colonizing drift logs.

name: Shunosaurus lii
currentFacts: Tail tipped with heavy bony club equipped with two spikes.
Complete skeletons exhibited in Zigong Dinosaur Museum.

name: Datousaurus bashanensis
currentFacts: Massive deep boxy skull with broad spoon teeth.

name: Agilisaurus louderbacki
currentFacts: Complete skeleton preserving clear bipedal proportions.

name: Huayangosaurus taibaii
currentFacts: Retained premaxillary teeth in front of snout.

name: Protoceratops andrewsi
currentFacts: Found in combat lock with Velociraptor ('Fighting Dinosaurs' specimen).
Broad neck frill without horn brows.

name: Pinacosaurus grangeri
currentFacts: Mass juvenile bonebeds buried by desert sandstorms.

name: Tarbosaurus bataar
currentFacts: Proportionally smallest 2-fingered arms of any tyrannosaurid.

name: Therizinosaurus cheloniformis
currentFacts: Enormous 1-meter long scythe claws on forelimbs.
Largest claws of any land animal in history.

name: Gallimimus bullatus
currentFacts: Slender sprinting limbs built for high speed.

name: Lufengosaurus huenei
currentFacts: First dinosaur displayed on a Chinese postage stamp.

name: Indosaurus matleyi
currentFacts: Thickened skull roof with small hornlets.

name: Barapasaurus tagorei
currentFacts: One of the earliest true sauropods in the world.

name: Spinosaurus aegyptiacus
currentFacts: 1.8m tall dorsal sail supported by neural spines.
Paddle-like tail for active swimming propel.

name: Carcharodontosaurus saharicus
currentFacts: 1.6m long skull with 20 cm shark-like serrated teeth.

name: Heterodontosaurus tucki
currentFacts: Three distinct tooth types: incisors, canine tusks, and cheek teeth.

name: Kunbarrasaurus ieversae
currentFacts: Most complete fossil skeleton found in Australia.
Preserved stomach contents (seeds, leaves, fern sporangia).

name: Jingshanosaurus myankouensis
currentFacts: One of the last large prosauropods.
Complete skeleton with skull exhibited in Kunming.

name: Bienosaurus lufengensis
currentFacts: Rows of bony osteoderms on back.

name: Lukousaurus yini
currentFacts: Small predatory archosaur with horn-like nasal crests.

name: Eshanosaurus deguchiianus
currentFacts: Left dentary jaw bone with specialized herbivorous teeth.
Extends coelurosaur lineage into Early Jurassic.

name: Sinosaurus triassicus
currentFacts: Apex predator of Early Jurassic China.
Pair of double crests on top of head like Dilophosaurus.

name: Isisaurus colberti
currentFacts: Short vertical neck with robust forelimbs.

name: Dandakosaurus indicus
currentFacts: Apex theropod predator of Kota Formation.

name: Treposuchus indicus
currentFacts: Elongated snout filled with needle teeth.

name: Sivapithecus sivalensis
currentFacts: Concave facial profile and tall oval eye sockets.
Thick tooth enamel for crushing tough seeds.

name: Gigantopithecus bilaspurensis
currentFacts: Massive lower jaw with huge grinding molars.

name: Bramatherium megacephalum
currentFacts: Five crown ossicones forming a helmet crest.

name: Hexaprotodon sivalensis
currentFacts: Primitive hippopotamus with 6 incisors instead of 4.

name: Bahariasaurus ingens
currentFacts: Rivaled Spinosaurus and Carcharodontosaurus in length.

name: Aegyptosaurus baharijensis
currentFacts: Found in coastal mangrove swamp deposits.
Fossils also destroyed in Munich 1944 bombing.

name: Abrictosaurus consors
currentFacts: Early heterodontosaurid without prominent upper tusks.

name: Mamenchisaurus constructus
currentFacts: Extremely long neck making up half of body length.

name: Shuvuuia deserti
currentFacts: Single stout claw on short arms for digging anthills.

name: Homalocephale calathocercos
currentFacts: Broad pelvis for live birth or large digestive tract.

name: Prenocephale prenes
currentFacts: Thick domed skull roof surrounded by bony spikes.

name: Lametasaurus indicus
currentFacts: Armor osteoderms found associated with theropod bones.

name: Kotaichthys kartikeyai
currentFacts: Found in Kota limestone beds of Telangana.

name: Indobatrachus pusillus
currentFacts: Preserved complete skeleton in lake shale.

name: Paralititan stromeri
currentFacts: Found in coastal mangrove tidal flat deposits.

name: Blikanasaurus cromptoni
currentFacts: Heavy stocky quadrupedal sauropodomorph lower limb.

name: Spinosaurus maroccanus
currentFacts: Moroccan spinosaur species based on cervical vertebrae length.

name: Yangchuanosaurus shangyouensis
currentFacts: Apex carnosaur predator of Late Jurassic China.
Rugged facial crests on top of nose.

name: Opisthocoelicaudia skarzynskii
currentFacts: Opposite cavity tail vertebrae for rigid tripod stance.

name: Eocarcharia dinops
currentFacts: Heavy brow ridge over eye socket.
Bladelike serrated teeth for flesh cutting.

name: Chungkingosaurus jiangbeiensis
currentFacts: Smallest known stegosaurid from Shaximiao Formation.
Multiple pairs of thagomizer tail spikes.

name: Squalicorax falcatus
geographicRange: {"continent":"North America, Europe, Africa","region":"Western Interior Seaway","country":"United States","fossilFormation":"Niobrara Formation"}
currentFacts: Known as the 'Crow Shark' due to its ubiquitous presence as a scavenger in Cretaceous seas.
Fossilized Squalicorax teeth have been found embedded in the bones of terrestrial dinosaurs, proving it scavenged on carcasses washed out to sea.
Possessed distinctive serrated, crescent-shaped teeth perfect for slicing through tough flesh and bone.

name: Zalmoxes robustus
currentFacts: Lived on Hațeg Island, an isolated landmass in Late Cretaceous Europe, leading to insular dwarfism.
Possessed a surprisingly robust, heavy skull compared to its small overall body size.
Served as a primary herbivorous prey species for the giant azhdarchid pterosaur Hatzegopteryx.

name: Geosaurus giganteus
currentFacts: Completely lost heavy osteoderm armor to maximize aquatic agility and swimming speed.
Transformed its legs into hydrofoil paddles and developed a fish-like hypocercal tail fin.
Equipped with serrated, ziphodont teeth optimized for tearing prey rather than crushing shells.

name: Metriorhynchus geoffroyii
geographicRange: {"continent":"Europe","region":"English Channel Basin","country":"United Kingdom, France","fossilFormation":"Oxford Clay Formation"}
currentFacts: Possessed large salt glands positioned above its eyes to excrete excess ocean salt.
Gave live birth at sea (viviparity) as its limbs could no longer support walking on land.
Had smooth skin without armor scales, reducing drag in the water.

name: Megaraptor namunhuaiquii
currentFacts: Its famous 35 cm sickle claw was originally misidentified as a giant foot claw like Velociraptor's.
Head of the enigmatic Megaraptora clade, which dominated South American ecosystems after carcharodontosaurids declined.
Possessed highly pneumatic (air-filled) bones, making it agile for an 8-meter long predator.

name: Maip macrothorax
currentFacts: Named 'Maip' after an evil mythological spirit of the Aonikenk (Tehuelche) people representing cold death.
The largest megaraptoran ever discovered, outsizing Megaraptor and Australovenator.
Had an unusually wide, heavy thoracic cavity ('macrothorax') housing large lung systems for high metabolism.

name: Lythronax argestes
currentFacts: Nickname 'Gore King' comes from its scientific name translating directly to 'King of Gore'.
Possessed broad skull rear and narrow snout, giving it overlapping 3D binocular vision like T. rex 13 million years earlier.
Proved that tyrannosaurid radiation occurred much earlier than previously assumed.

name: Moros intrepidus
currentFacts: Filled the 70-million-year gap in North American tyrannosaur evolution.
Existed as a small, nimble predator when giant allosauroids (like Siats) were apex predators.
Extremely long leg bones indicate superior running speed and cursorial agility.

name: Sauroposeidon proteles
geographicRange: {"continent":"North America","region":"Gulf Coast / Interior Plains","country":"United States","fossilFormation":"Antlers Formation, Cloverly Formation"}
currentFacts: Its neck reached up to 12 meters (39 feet) in length, accounting for over one-third of its total body length.
Cervical vertebrae were up to 1.4 meters long and filled with honeycombed internal air cells (trabecular bone).
Stood as tall as a 6-story building, allowing it to browse vegetation inaccessible to any other creature.

name: Psephoderma alpinum
currentFacts: Superficially resembled a marine turtle but belonged to the extinct placodont order of sauropterygians.
Had two distinct protective carapace shields: one covering the shoulders/chest and a smaller one over the pelvis.
Possessed toothless, narrow beaked jaws lined internally with flat, pavement-like crushing plates.

name: Vayuraptor agriculturalis
currentFacts: Coexisted with another medium-sized theropod, Siamraptor, in Early Cretaceous Thailand.
Ankle bones (astragalus and calcaneum) were fused together, enhancing biomechanical sprinting stability.
Species name 'agriculturalis' honors local farmers who assisted in uncovering the fossil site.

name: Rhizodus hibberti
currentFacts: Possessed enormous 22 cm (9 inch) tusk-like teeth anchored deeply into massive jaws.
Could likely lung onto land or shallow swamp margins to snatch terrestrial amphibians, similar to modern crocodiles.
Its skin was covered in heavy, overlapping cosmoid scales providing armor against rival aquatic predators.

name: Gillicus arcuatus
geographicRange: {"continent":"North America","region":"Western Interior Seaway","country":"United States","fossilFormation":"Smoky Hill Chalk"}
currentFacts: Best known as the swallowed prey in the famous 14-foot Xiphactinus specimen at Hays, Kansas.
Possessed numerous fine, needle-like gill rakers used to strain small marine organisms from sea water.
Had deeply embedded, thin circular scales that reduced turbulence during swift schooling swims.

name: Yutyrannus huali
currentFacts: Holds the record as the largest direct feather-bearing animal in Earth's history (9 meters long, 1.4 tonnes).
Feathers were 20 cm long filamentous proto-feathers providing insulation in Liaoning's chilly 10°C climate.
Possessed a high median crest along its snout used for species display and intra-species communication.

name: Nanotyrannus lancensis
currentFacts: Subject of one of the longest and most fiercely contested debates in paleontology history.
Had significantly more teeth (up to 36 in upper jaw) and larger forelimbs than adult T. rex.
Possessed extremely long, slender leg bones adapted for high-speed pursuit running.

name: Palaeoloxodon antiquus
geographicRange: {"continent":"Europe, Asia","region":"Mediterranean & Central Europe","country":"Germany, United Kingdom, Italy, Greece","fossilFormation":"Ebbsfleet Valley deposits"}
currentFacts: One of the largest terrestrial mammals to ever walk the Earth, outsizing the Woolly Mammoth.
Possessed long, nearly straight tusks reaching up to 3.8 meters in length.
Coexisted with Neanderthals and early Homo sapiens, who actively hunted these leviathans with wooden spears.

name: Gryposuchus colombianus
geographicRange: {"continent":"South America","region":"Amazon & Orinoco Basins","country":"Colombia, Venezuela, Brazil","fossilFormation":"La Venta Formation, Urumaco Formation"}
currentFacts: Possessed an extremely elongated, narrow snout packed with over 80 inter-locking needle teeth.
Inhabited the mega-wetlands of Miocene South America alongside giant caimans like Purussaurus.
The hook-like curvature at the tip of its snout helped hold onto slippery, armor-plated prehistoric catfish.

name: Plesiosuchus manselii
currentFacts: The largest metriorhynchid crocodilian ever discovered, outgrowing Geosaurus and Metriorhynchus.
Had wide-opening jaws with coarse serrations adapted for severing flesh from large marine vertebrates.
Shared marine habitats with Dakosaurus, dividing ecological niches based on skull mechanics.

name: Suchodus durobrivensis
geographicRange: {"continent":"Europe","region":"Oxford Clay Basin","country":"United Kingdom, France","fossilFormation":"Oxford Clay Formation"}
currentFacts: Possessed significantly shorter, stronger jaws than Metriorhynchus for crushing armored prey.
Equipped with paddle-shaped limbs and a tail fin for pelagic sea life.
Fossilized eye rings (sclerotic rings) show adaptations for deep diving.

name: Edestus heinrichi
geographicRange: {"continent":"North America, Europe","region":"Illinois Basin","country":"United States, Russia","fossilFormation":"Carbondale Formation"}
currentFacts: Did not shed worn teeth; new teeth grew in from the back, pushing old teeth forward into protruding curved brackets.
Jaws operated like a pair of hedge trimmers, thrashing up and down to slash prey.
Belonged to Eugeneodontida, closely related to modern chimaeras rather than true sharks.

name: Pyroraptor olympius
currentFacts: Named 'Fire Thief' because its fossils were uncovered immediately after a major forest fire.
Possessed a curved 6.5 cm sickle claw on the second toe of each foot for gripping prey.
Fully covered in feathers with wing-like plumage along its forelimbs.

name: Dracovenator regenti
currentFacts: One of the earliest apex theropod dinosaurs discovered in southern Africa.
Possessed paired bony crests running along the top of its skull.
Targeted abundant early sauropodomorph dinosaurs as primary prey.

name: Sarcosaurus woodi
currentFacts: One of the earliest true Jurassic theropod dinosaurs discovered in the UK.
Possessed a small nasal horn or crest similar to Ceratosaurus.
Inhabited coastal mudflats alongside early marine reptiles.

name: Animantarx ramaljonesi
currentFacts: First dinosaur discovered exclusively via radiological radiation detection technology.
Possessed a heavily armored skull with small horn-like projections behind the eyes.
Lacked a tail club, relying instead on shoulder spikes and fused armor plates.

name: Segnosaurus galbinensis
currentFacts: Bizarre theropod that evolved away from meat-eating to become a strict herbivore.
Possessed a massive pot belly to ferment tough plant vegetation.
Equipped with elongated, curved hand claws used to pull down tree branches.

name: Bajadasaurus pronuspinax
currentFacts: Possessed extremely long, thin neural spines along its neck that curved forward over its head.
The neck spines were likely covered in keratin sheaths, acting as defensive spikes against predators while grazing.
Eyes were positioned high on its skull, allowing it to look out for predators while lowering its snout to eat.

name: Fukuiraptor kitadaniensis
currentFacts: Initially thought to be a dromaeosaurid due to a large hand claw, later recognized as a megaraptoran.
The state dinosaur mascot of Fukui Prefecture, Japan.
Possessed large hand claws used to grasp prey.

name: Fukuisaurus tetoriensis
currentFacts: Skull lacked the kinetic flexibility seen in advanced hadrosaurs, chewing with a rigid maxilla.
Coexisted with Fukuiraptor, Fukuititan, and Koshisaurus in Early Cretaceous Japan.
Equipped with a sharp beak for clipping tough vegetation.

name: Leedsichthys problematicus
geographicRange: {"continent":"Europe, South America","region":"Tethys / Boreal Oceans","country":"United Kingdom, France, Germany, Chile","fossilFormation":"Oxford Clay Formation"}
currentFacts: Holds the record as the largest bony fish in Earth's history, rivaling modern baleen whales in ecological role.
Possessed over 40,000 delicate mesh-like gill raker teeth to filter microscopic plankton.
Bite marks on Leedsichthys fins show it was hunted by giant marine predators like Liopleurodon and Metriorhynchus.

name: Suchomimus tenerensis
currentFacts: Possessed a narrow 1.2-meter long crocodile-like skull lined with 100 conical teeth.
Had a massive 30 cm sickle claw on its thumb used to spear fish.
Featured a low neural spine sail reaching up to 60 cm high along its back.

name: Oxalaia quilombensis
currentFacts: Named after Oxalá, the principal deity in the Afro-Brazilian Candomblé pantheon.
The largest carnivorous dinosaur recorded from Brazil.
Close relative of North African Spinosaurus, featuring double functional replacement teeth.

name: Tropaeognathus mesembrinus
currentFacts: One of the largest pre-azhdarchid flying reptiles known, with an 8.2-meter wingspan.
Possessed large convex keel-like crests on the tips of both upper and lower jaws.
Crests acted as rudders to stabilize jaws while dipping into water at high speed to catch fish.

name: Coloborhynchus clavirostris
currentFacts: Featured a unique flattened front snout tip with teeth projecting forward at odd angles.
Equipped with a prominent crest along the front upper jaw.
Earliest recognized anhanguerid pterosaur in the European fossil record.

name: Arctodus simus
geographicRange: {"continent":"North America","region":"Great Plains & Coastlines","country":"United States, Canada, Mexico","fossilFormation":"Rancho La Brea tar pits, Riverbluff Cave"}
currentFacts: Stood over 3.4 meters (11 feet) tall on its hind legs, making it the largest terrestrial mammalian carnivore in North America.
Used its massive size to bully smaller predators like saber-toothed cats (Smilodon) away from fresh kills.
Possessed unusually long, slender legs allowing it to pace efficiently across vast distances.

name: Purussaurus brasiliensis
geographicRange: {"continent":"South America","region":"Amazon Basin","country":"Brazil, Peru, Venezuela","fossilFormation":"Solimões Formation, Urumaco Formation"}
currentFacts: Possessed one of the strongest bite forces of any animal in Earth's history (~69,000 Newtons / 7 tonnes force).
Its massive skull measured 1.4 meters long and was immensely broad for crushing thick mammalian bones.
Consumed over 40 kilograms of meat per day to maintain its giant metabolic needs.

name: Josephoartigasia monesi
geographicRange: {"continent":"South America","region":"Rio de la Plata Basin","country":"Uruguay","fossilFormation":"San José Formation"}
currentFacts: Holds the Guinness World Record as the largest rodent to ever exist on Earth.
Possessed enormous 30 cm incisors with a bite force equivalent to a tiger, used for digging or defense.
Replaced traditional ungulate herbivore niches in prehistoric South American river estuaries.

name: Livyatan melvillei
currentFacts: Possessed the largest functional biting teeth of any known animal in Earth's history (36 cm long and 12 cm wide).
Unlike modern sperm whales which feed on squid using toothless upper jaws, Livyatan had huge teeth in BOTH upper and lower jaws.
Coexisted and directly competed with Megalodon for marine mammalian prey in Miocene oceans.

name: Kelenken guillermoi
currentFacts: Possessed the largest head of any known bird in history, with a skull measuring 71.6 cm (28 inches) long.
Could sprint at estimated speeds exceeding 45 km/h to run down prehistoric mammals.
Killed prey by striking downwards with its massive eagle-like hooked beak like an axe.

name: Varanus priscus
currentFacts: The largest terrestrial venomous squamate reptile in Earth's history.
Possessed venom glands in its lower jaws similar to its smaller living relative, the Komodo Dragon.
Serrated recumbent teeth allowed it to tear open heavy hide of giant extinct marsupials.

name: Daeodon shoshonensis
geographicRange: {"continent":"North America","region":"Great Plains","country":"United States","fossilFormation":"Arikaree Group (Agate Fossil Beds)"}
currentFacts: Nicknamed the 'Hell Pig', though genetically closer to hippos and whales than true pigs.
Possessed a massive 90 cm (3 foot) skull with heavy bony cheek flanges (jugal flanges) for muscle attachment.
Heavily worn teeth show it routinely cracked open giant animal bones to extract nutrient-rich marrow.
